title: Private rollforward controller and LTS compatibility harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a rollforward controller and compatibility harness to enable safe, orchestrated upgrades for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). This ticket covers the controller that coordinates multi-stage migrations (schema, binary, runtime config), the compatibility graph used to map feasible rollforward/rollback paths across LTS and minor channels, and the on-prem-friendly packaging+signing model for offline upgrades. The goal is deterministic, auditable, and recoverable upgrades that respect tenant isolation, resource constraints, and air-gapped environments.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can create and execute a staged rollout plan that includes: preflight checks, canary cohorts, parallelism controls, and automated rollback triggers

Compatibility harness produces a migration graph that proves at least one safe path from any supported older LTS to target release and can generate fallback variants when direct upgrade is incompatible
Signed migration bundles can be consumed by on-prem agents without internet access and validate signatures against customer KMS or bundled root keys
End-to-end tests pass in the upgrade simulator for >95% of synthetic tenant topologies and detect common KV/schema-incompatibilities
Telemetry emits per-tenant step latencies, failure classifications, and pre/post-data-consistency checks to the console
tasks: Design compatibility graph data model and persistence (CRD + compact index)
Implement rollforward-controller: reconcile upgrade CR -> staged jobs, cohort selection, and canary gating
Add preflight probes: traffic-mirroring dry-run, KV checksum, schema compatibility checkers
Create offline bundle signer and verifier with KMS/HSM integration option
Implement migration dry-run harness and deterministic simulation mode
Integrate with Console to display per-tenant rollout status, risk score, and allowed rollback operations
Create automated smoke tests and chaos scenarios for rollback validation
comments: 2026-02-16: Initial RFC posted. Key trade-offs discussed: heavy upfront compatibility graph vs. on-demand compatibility checks. Decision: build incremental graph that is updated during model onboarding to keep queries fast for large customer fleets.
2026-02-22: Design review with PM/Infra. Action item: add explicit resource quota checks per cohort and a batch size limiter to prevent saturating on-prem GPU hosts.

2026-03-01: Prototype controller reconciler implemented. Early tests show deterministic dry-run catching a KV cache hotkey mismatch on a mock model upgrade. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrades/pull/412
2026-03-05: Security review kickoff. Offline signer needs HSM-backed key option; security requested threat model for signed bundles in air-gapped installs.

2026-03-10: QA report: simulator passes 94% of generated topologies. Remaining failures are due to legacy schema migrations that require two-phase column backfills. Follow-up: design dual-write shim and small-blocking window plan.
rollout_plan: 1) Publish migration bundle and compatibility proof to staging; 2) Run deterministic dry-run against snapshot of staging tenants; 3) Canary 5% of fleets with health checks enabled for 30m; 4) Expand cohorts with linear ramp controlled by resource quota checks; 5) Finalize when 95% success and no data-consistency regressions; 6) Post-rollout validation sweep and sign-off
migration_playbook: Preflight: run schema compatibility, KV checksum, and traffic mirror dry-run. If any step fails, controller halts and captures snapshot. Canary phase: deploy to single tenant cluster with telemetry hooks and automated rollback on data-consistency or error budget breaches. Rollback strategy: apply reverse migration using pre-computed fallback variant; if binary rollback is unsafe, isolate traffic and run read-only failover. Emergency path: operator can trigger snapshot-restore from controller UI with documented operator steps.
notes: We intentionally avoid in-place destructive schema migrations in the first rollout wave. Instead we prefer additive migrations and background backfills via a dual-write shim. For long-lived customers with strict change windows, we will support operator-scheduled maintenance with manual cohort approval.
implementation_notes: Controller is implemented as a Kubernetes operator in Go. Compatibility graph stored in an index-backed CRD that supports O(log n) queries by (fromVersion,toVersion). Offline bundles are tar.gz with signed manifest, migration plan JSON, and optional ephemeral container images for environments that permit local image caching.
qa_and_testing: Simulator harness uses replayed request traces from anonymized customers and injects failure modes (disk pressure, network partitions, CPU throttling). CI includes an 'upgrade-simulation' pipeline that runs every PR touching the controller and blocks merges on new regressions.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: on-prem resource heterogeneity could cause rollout slowdowns. Mitigation: cohort selection based on observed capacity metrics and configurable concurrency. Risk: signed bundles rejected in air-gapped installs due to missing root key. Mitigation: provide documented root key onboarding flow and offline root key rotation utility.
follow_up: Post-release items: (a) integrate upgrade insights into Optimize to recommend batching changes for cost-sensitive upgrades, (b) add automated policy-driven schedule windows for enterprise customers, (c) expand graph to include model-variant compatibility metadata
